findings.title: Malformed percent encoding can suppress a valid scanner finding
findings.failure_condition: A scanned text contains any malformed percent sequence before or beside a valid percent-encoded credential URI. decodeURIComponent is applied to the whole view, throws, and the catch/break path skips the decoded view instead of failing closed or decoding safe segments.

reproduction.method: Call production canonicalizeScannerInput and scanCanonicalContent with a synthetic malformed percent prefix and a separately encoded synthetic database credential URI.
reproduction.expected: A CREDENTIAL_URI finding or an explicit fail-closed canonicalization finding.

findings.impact: An attacker can place one malformed percent token in an otherwise scanned text to conceal a credential that the declared percent-decoding contract would detect in isolation.
findings.required_resolution: Canonicalize percent-encoded input segment-wise or emit a blocking malformed-encoding finding without abandoning other canonical views. Add differential tests combining malformed encodings with every in-contract credential class.

findings.title: The filed scanner fixture oracle does not enforce the full declared header and binary matrix
findings.failure_condition: The formal Phase 1 fixture suite passes without asserting all nine declared binary signatures, safe binary negatives, extension/magic mismatches, or the complete quoted Set-Cookie, session, and token header families through the production scanner path.

reproduction.method: Compare the declared scanner contract and production recognizers with the exact fixture-suite manifest and runner assertions.
reproduction.observed: The independent reviewer matrix exercises cases absent from the filed 50-case oracle; that oracle can stay green if an uncovered recognizer regresses.

findings.impact: The filed suite is not a trustworthy regression boundary for controls claimed by the candidate, so a later change can silently remove an advertised finding class while all authoritative fixture totals remain green.
findings.required_resolution: Make the formal suite table-driven from the scanner contract and require exact positive and negative coverage for every declared binary magic, mismatch, quoted-header, session, cookie, token, URL-safe entropy, and canonicalization composition class.

a4_closure_entries.reason: The unified canonicalization pipeline still has a composition bypass: one malformed percent sequence suppresses a valid decoded finding.
The retained implementation has bounded header and binary recognition with explicit extension and magic handling; no direct implementation bypass from the A4 construction remained.
The filed contract is versioned and bounded, uses exact manifest and file-set identity, and does not claim OS isolation or general DLP.
The formal fixture oracle still does not lock the entire scanner contract matrix despite the production recognizers being present.

candidate_review_gate_recommendation.reason: A scanner composition bypass remains and the formal fixture oracle does not prove the complete declared scanner contract.

residual_risks: Agent and reviewer identity is procedural rather than cryptographic.
Agent path policy is not an OS sandbox.
The scanner is bounded deterministic detection, not DLP or repository-global sensitive-data assurance.
External executables, child-process invocation, PowerShell or cmd behavior, parent-process override and TOCTOU remain outside the claimed isolation boundary.
An unstaged working tree remains a human-reviewed residual risk and is not proof of staged commit identity.
